text:
The 30-year costs more in total interest. One correction to my earlier line: the starting balance is the same, but it pays down more slowly, so it stays higher for longer.

Example at 6% on $300,000: the 30-year totals about $347,500 in interest and the 15-year about $155,700. The 15-year payment is higher (about $2,532 vs. $1,799 a month). In practice 15-year loans usually carry a lower rate, which widens the gap further.
